skill.name: convex-monitor
skill.description: Monitor typed Convex development and production events, then guide the next appropriate response.
skill.summary: Wait for the next Convex event and respond according to its type.
skill.author: get-convex

security_audit.summary: The only static alert is a false positive caused by Markdown backticks around a tool name. No command execution or malicious intent is present.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 14 uses Markdown backticks to format the wait_for_event tool name. It contains no Ruby expression, shell command, or command execution instruction.

content.value_statement: Convex teams need a reliable way to react to the next important development or production event. This skill waits for typed events and directs the response.
actual_capabilities: Calls wait_for_event with a project directory, event kinds, and timeout.
Waits for the first event from local errors, deployment subscriptions, or Sentinel production errors.
Routes Convex errors, production errors, feature requests, and quiet heartbeats to distinct actions.
Uses a polling fallback when blocking MCP support is unavailable.
Preserves the same fixed, versioned event contract across blocking and polling mechanisms.
limitations: Requires a harness that provides wait_for_event or the described polling fallback.
Production error monitoring requires a deployed Convex cloud application and Sentinel.
Monitors the next event rather than reviewing complete historical logs.
Fix quality depends on the available project context and development tools.

use_cases.title: Resolve the Next Development Error
use_cases.description: Wait for a local Convex error, decode it, and begin a focused repair.

use_cases.title: Triage a Production Failure
use_cases.description: Watch Sentinel for the next production error and start a structured investigation.

use_cases.title: Process Incoming Feature Requests
use_cases.description: Wait for a typed feature request and use it as the next implementation task.

prompt_templates.title: Watch My Convex Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Monitor the Convex project at [project directory] for the next error or feature request. Report the event and take the appropriate action.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start basic monitoring with default event types.

prompt_templates.title: Wait for a Development Error
prompt_templates.prompt: Watch [project directory] for the next Convex development error for [timeout]. Decode the error, identify its cause, and propose a focused fix.
prompt_templates.scenario: Investigate the next local development failure.

prompt_templates.title: Triage the Next Production Error
prompt_templates.prompt: Monitor [project directory] for the next Sentinel production error. Summarize impact, locate the likely source, and implement a verified repair.
prompt_templates.scenario: Respond to an incident in a deployed Convex application.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Continuous Event Response Loop
prompt_templates.prompt: Continuously monitor [project directory] for [event kinds]. Handle each event by type, verify completed work, and resume after quiet heartbeats.
prompt_templates.scenario: Coordinate repeated event handling with a defined event filter.

output_examples.input: Watch the current project for the next development error.
output_examples.output: Detected a Convex development error. The response identifies the failing operation, explains the likely cause, and outlines a focused repair.

output_examples.input: Monitor production errors through Sentinel and triage the next event.
output: Event: Production error received through Sentinel.
Triage: Impact and probable source are summarized.
Action: A repair and verification approach are prepared.

output_examples.input: Wait for errors or feature requests, then continue after quiet periods.
output_examples.output: No matching event arrived before the timeout. Monitoring resumes after the quiet heartbeat.

best_practices: Specify the project directory, desired event kinds, and a practical timeout.
Use the blocking tool when available to avoid unnecessary polling.
Verify each repair with relevant tests before resuming the monitoring loop.
anti_patterns: Do not monitor production errors without a deployed application and Sentinel.
Do not treat a quiet heartbeat as evidence that the application is healthy.
Do not implement feature requests without reviewing requirements and project context.

faq.question: What events can this skill handle?
faq.answer: It handles Convex errors, next errors, production errors, feature requests, and quiet heartbeats.

faq.question: Does this skill provide the monitoring tool?
faq.answer: No. The execution harness must provide wait_for_event or support the polling fallback.

faq.question: Can it monitor production errors?
faq.answer: Yes. Production monitoring requires a deployed Convex cloud application and Sentinel.

faq.question: What happens when no event arrives?
faq.answer: The workflow receives a quiet heartbeat and can continue waiting.

faq.question: Does it work without blocking MCP support?
faq.answer: Yes. The described fallback uses polling while preserving the same typed event contract.

faq.question: Does it automatically fix every error?
faq.answer: No. It directs diagnosis and repair, but success depends on project context, available tools, and verification.
